quest.title: The Contestant
quest.description: You meet Dori again. Ask her if she knows something else...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It's time yet again for an information sale from Lord Sangemah Bay!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Would you two like to purchase the latest reports? Let me see, this information isn't that important so it'll go for only half a million Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It's half the usual price. What a bargain!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mind giving it to me for free?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Whoa, you want to bring it down to zero Mora. Just as I expected...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: But, I am the great Lord Sangemah Bay. Well, since you're so interested, I'll tell you for free, but you must keep it to yourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I heard that twenty years ago, there was a contestant whose personality suddenly changed after taking part in the competition!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, it looks like someone saw him in Aaru Village. I wonder where he ended up?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: That's all the information you're getting for free. If you want to hear more, you gotta pay two million Mora. I appreciate your patronage!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a rip off! We can just go to Aaru Village ourselves and ask around!

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Twenty years ago... a young man did appear here.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Back then, life was much harder than it is now. Poverty, disease, ignorance... They tormented us constantly.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: That young man, clearly from the Akademiya with a bright future, was nevertheless willing to come here and help us.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: He taught us how to deal with Wenut and monsters. He bought us a lot of medicine with money from his own pocket and took care of the ill all by himself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He sounds like a great guy!

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Yeah... Too bad the good die young.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: He was always frowning, and no one knew what he was worried about. Everyone was wondering if he was going to leave us. This place did not have the means to properly host him.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Still, many said he was a bit crazy to begin with. For example, he would sometimes tell children a story about how, as a child, he taught a strange creature to write.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Later, he would often leave the village and explore the desert. Once, I asked him what he was looking for, and he said he wanted to talk to someone from the Nagarsomething group.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Later on, I heard that he died in the quicksand. It is said that he encountered a caravan trapped in quicksand on his way to investigate something. He saved many people but he himself was unable to get out in time...

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: At that time, there was still a half-finished letter addressed to his child at home. After he died, my son took that letter with him, thinking about delivering it someday.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that unfinished letter... still here?

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: No. It's not here...

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: To live a better life, my son became a mercenary. He was killed in a scuffle a few years ago, and his belongings were taken.

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Many years have passed in the blink of an eye. I wonder how his child turned out, and if they hold a grudge against him?

dialogues.speaker: Rishti
dialogues.text: Not many people know these things anymore. I'm getting old. Perhaps, I'll forget these things soon, too.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Mm, you've realized it too, haven't you?
